failure_families: large high-contrast density islands and saturated highlight patches on the Nikon packaging row
autonomous_visual_review.notes: The shared-density projection materially removes the widespread coloured salt texture seen in P4GR and keeps most rows close to AO6. It nevertheless produces conspicuous yellow/white patch islands on the Nikon row, while the Blackmagic row also requires excessive analytical limiting. The failure is localized rather than population-wide, but remains a severe-artifact veto.

scientific_conclusion: A single common optical-density residual is a useful chroma-correlation mechanism: it reduces population p95 absolute deviation from 0.05868 in P4GR to 0.00404 and removes the broad chromatic-speckle failure. It is still not safe because high-contrast density islands survive on one photographic row and one other row requires 14.41% limiting. The next mechanism must make stochastic structure density- and scale-aware before projection, rather than tune this residual or its gates.
next_leaf: Develop a density-conditioned subpixel LOD field that suppresses unresolved particle excursions before common-density projection, then test on this consumed cohort before any fresh confirmation.
claim_ceiling: Consumed nine-camera CC0 relative-display photographic mechanism development only; not independent confirmation, scene exposure, calibrated film, stock response, human preference or product promotion.
